body:
Etymology

From dentdelyon , from dent de lion , also in dēns leōnis , referring to the jagged shape of the plant's leaves. The term is now rare in French (together with liondent, calque from Germanic), but compare , , , , , , all descendants, calques, or loan translations of the Latin term.

Displaced various words, including native , native , and and swine's snout and mostly displaced , monk's head , and pissabed .

Noun

Any of the several species of plant in the genus , characterised by yellow flower heads and notched, broad-ended leaves, especially the common dandelion ( ).

The flower head or fruiting head of the dandelion plant.

A yellow colour, like that of the flower.

Adjective

Of a yellow colour, like that of the flower.
